answer: In a decentralized economy, the Byzantine Fault Tolerance (BFT) consensus algorithm can be employed to resist fake-identity attacks. This algorithm establishes a bridge between honest agents, forming a mesa of trusted peers. Each agent verifies the identities of its neighbors, preventing malicious agents from creating a single, dominating identity. This approach is akin to the fable of the ant and the grasshopper, where cooperation and mutual verification lead to a resilient system, whereas a single attacker can be isolated and removed, ensuring the integrity of the network.
